cards.text: The next day, the great crowd in town for the feast hears that Jesus is coming to Jerusalem. Friend, that news moves faster than a group chat after somebody texts “Big news. Call me.” Nobody stays home for this one.

cards.question: The crowd grabs ___ branches and goes out to meet Jesus.

cards.text: Out they go, and they are LOUD. “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”

cards.question: The crowd going out to meet Jesus also shouts that He is the King of Israel.

cards.text: So the crowd is calling Him King, and a King coming into Jerusalem needs a ride. Me, I'd make my big entrance hopping on my gold base. Hop. Hop. Hop. I'd get there NEXT Tuesday.

cards.question: Jesus finds a young ___ and sits on it.
John says Jesus sat on that young donkey just as something said He would. What?
Those written words speak to the Daughter of Zion about her King coming on a donkey's colt. What do they tell her?

cards.text: Here are the words: “Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion. See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey.” Written down long before, and here He is, riding in just like it says.

cards.question: The disciples are right there for all of this. True or false: they understand what it means right away.

cards.text: Not at first, friend. It clicks for them later, the way a joke finally hits me three days after somebody told it, and I'm laughing alone in the bakery at nothing.

cards.question: The disciples remember what was done to Jesus and realize it was written about Him after He was ___.

cards.text: Meanwhile, some people in this crowd were with Jesus the day He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.

cards.question: What do the people who saw Jesus raise Lazarus keep doing?
John gives another reason the crowd went out to meet Jesus. What is it?

answers.text: They heard He would be crowned
They heard He was giving gifts

cards.text: Then the Pharisees, a group of Jewish religious leaders, huddle up and talk it over with one another. And I bet this is not the day they had planned.

cards.question: Watching the crowd, the Pharisees tell one another that what they are doing against Jesus is working.

cards.text: Not even close: “You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!” That's me promising myself I'll only taste ONE chocolate chip. Doing me no good either, friend.

findings.problem: The passage opens with "The next day" but the opening card never says the day after what. John 12:1-11 has Jesus at the dinner in Bethany, where Mary anoints Him. The baker gets no context for where this moment falls.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: "Nobody stays home for this one" is stated as a fact about the crowd. John 12:12-13 says only that the great crowd heard the news and went out. No one is said to have stayed or gone beyond that crowd.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card cites John 12:14 but tells nothing from that verse. It is only setup and a joke. It also gives a practical reason for the donkey ("a King coming into Jerusalem needs a ride"). The text gives Scripture as the reason ("as it is written").

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card adds a reason the text doesn't give for why Jesus sat on the donkey (He "needs a ride").

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Card 8 has just taught the content of John 12:15 (do not be afraid, Daughter of Zion, your King on a donkey's colt). Card 9 restates the same verse right after it and moves nothing forward. It is a recap.
"Written down long before" adds a time the passage doesn't give. John 12:14-15 says only "as it is written."

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "Some people in this crowd" changes the text in two ways. John 12:17 says "many people," not some. The text also doesn't place these witnesses inside the crowd that went out to meet Him. Verse 18 speaks of "the crowd" separately, and the passage leaves open how the two groups connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup line "I bet this is not the day they had planned" tells the baker things aren't going the Pharisees' way. That rules out True on card 17 before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't share the core action. In John 12:19 the Pharisees are failing to stop others from going after Jesus. In the joke, Papa Dorin is failing to stop himself from eating chips. The image also casts Jesus in the place of the temptation he's trying to resist, which sits poorly with the reverence rule.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
